history.summary: IDENTITY AMBIGUITY: the CSV row 'Swaminarayan Temple, Anand' is a generic listing with no address or sect, and no single temple could be conclusively matched to it. Anand town and its surroundings host several Swaminarayan temples of different sects: the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir at Goya Talav (documented in seq 299) and the six-storey BAPS mandir in the heart of Anand town (seq 1457), Vadtal Sansthan temples in nearby villages (e.g. Palaj, Sojitra, Umreth), and the historic Vadtal Dham headquarters ~13 km away in Kheda district (not Anand district). This file documents the generic in-town Swaminarayan mandir per Gujarat Tourism / Holidify listings, dedicated to Lord Swaminarayan; it may duplicate seq 299 and seq 1457, which may all refer to the same BAPS mandir. Founding date, sect and exact address are UNVERIFIED. Coordinates are a town-level approximation for Anand.

town_description: Anand is a city in central Gujarat known as the Milk Capital of India, home of Amul and the birthplace of India's White Revolution. It is a major rail junction on the Mumbai-Ahmedabad line and adjoins the Vallabh Vidyanagar educational hub. The Charotar region around it is known for its prosperous farming communities and many temples.
